requirements.evidence: .env.example sets APP_NAME=PegaFila / APP_LOCALE=pt_BR; phpunit.xml:22-24 pins the three env values; config/mail.php:129-134 'theme' => 'pegafila'; pegafila.css .button-primary uses #0f7490 (the action button, so the color survives inlining); lang/pt_BR.json adds "Reset your password" and "Verify your email address"; routes/web.php:16-31 defines all five named routes with guest, throttle:6,1 and auth+signed+throttle; PasswordResetLinkController::store always returns back()->with('status', __('passwords.sent')); NewPasswordController::store rotates remember_token, fires PasswordReset and redirects to '/'; VerifyEmailController uses EmailVerificationRequest (403 on mismatch) and redirects to '/'; reset-password view has one e-mail input.

conventions.evidence: Inline $request->validate for the single-field forgot form and a Form Request (NewPasswordRequest) for the three-field reset, as the conventions require; PHPDoc on public methods; CHANGELOG updated under [Unreleased]. Deviations: forgot-password.blade.php and reset-password.blade.php each repeat the full HTML document, head and Vite/CDN block (lines 1-15) and no Blade component is extracted. The password write is inline in the controller closure, not in an app/Actions class, but it is not a domain write and the closure is Laravel's standard reset callback.

security.evidence: Forgot flow returns the same status for existing and unknown addresses (PasswordResetLinkController.php:27-32) and is throttled; reset validates token/email/password with Password::min(8)->letters()->mixedCase()->numbers() and confirmed; remember_token is rotated; verification uses auth + signed + EmailVerificationRequest; all view output uses {{ }} (token, old('email', $email)). Minor note: the fallback loads Bulma from a CDN without SRI, but only when no Vite build exists.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/Auth/PasswordResetTest.php covers the form markup, guest-only redirect, sent and unknown-address responses (same status, nothing sent), invalid e-mail, throttle 429, single e-mail input, a successful reset (hash, remember_token rotation, PasswordReset event, redirect '/'), an invalid token, a token used for another user, confirmation, and a dataset of weak passwords. VerifyEmailTest covers success, a wrong hash, another user's id and an unsigned link. AccountEmailsTest checks the config pins, the theme, pt-BR subjects/greeting/button/body/sub-copy with not->toContain('having trouble'), and the inlined #0f7490.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses Laravel's Password broker, EmailVerificationRequest and the stock notifications; only the two missing JSON strings are added. pegafila.css copies the whole 297-line default theme to change one color, which Laravel themes need in practice. The two views duplicate their page shell.

readability.evidence: Small controllers with clear names and docblocks that explain non-obvious behavior (e.g. 'The response is the same whether or not the address exists'); tests have descriptive names; no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: The diff touches only the env/phpunit pins, mail config and theme, lang entries, the two auth views, the controllers/request, routes and tests, plus the CHANGELOG. No login, registration, layouts, ui.php or Docker changes.

issues.explanation: Both views repeat the full HTML shell and the Vite/CDN asset block instead of sharing it through a Blade component, against the convention to extract reusable markup.
The fallback loads Bulma 0.9.4 from jsdelivr without an integrity attribute; this is a third-party asset load on auth pages.
The whole default theme is copied to change the button color, which leaves a lot of vendor CSS to maintain; accepted because Laravel themes replace default.css rather than extend it.

review.summary: The change implements the pt-BR account e-mails with a pegafila mail theme, the guest-only password-reset flow and the signed verification route, all with Laravel's built-in broker and notifications, plus thorough feature tests for the success, failure, throttle and tamper paths. Every requirement and contract item is met with no scope creep. Only small convention nits remain: the page shell is duplicated in both views and the Bulma fallback is loaded from a CDN, so I would approve with nits.
